content: The Henry Street Settlement was one of the earliest settlement houses established in the United States. It was created to provide essential assistance services, with a particular focus on healthcare, to impoverished individuals and newly arrived immigrants. In 1989, it was officially recognized as a National Historic Landmark. To this day, it continues to offer support services to residents of New York City's Lower East Side. The Henry Street Settlement was founded in 1895 by two nurses, Lillian Wald and Mary Maud Brewster, at 265 Henry Street in Manhattan's Lower East Side. Lillian Wald, who was a nursing student at the Women’s Medical College in New York City, was asked to develop programs to assist the poor. She described the Lower East Side as a densely populated and culturally distinct area, referring to it as a vast crowded area, a foreign city within our own. Two years later, she established the Henry Street Settlement to provide improved nursing care and other forms of aid to immigrants and the impoverished population. In 1915, the Neighborhood Playhouse was established nearby. The Settlement was designated a National Historic Landmark in 1989. In 2007, it was one of over 530 arts and social service institutions in New York City to receive funding from a $30 million grant provided by the Carnegie Corporation, made possible through a donation by then-Mayor Michael Bloomberg. The Henry Street Settlement was initially housed in a federal-era townhouse. Over time, additional townhouses were acquired and maintained as part of the Settlement. This effort preserved a portion of the 1820s streetscape amidst the development of a densely populated tenement district. The Settlement continues to provide a wide range of support services to residents of the Lower East Side. It operates programs across 11 facilities, including the Abrons Arts Center. These programs encompass arts classes for both children and adults, shelter services, healthcare services, senior services, workforce development initiatives, daycare centers, and after-school and summer youth programs. The Henry Street Settlement has served many clients who later achieved significant success in their respective fields. One notable example is Aaron Rabinowitz, a prominent figure in New York City's commercial real estate sector.
